name.oewn-14462254-n.tone: The plainest word for how others see a person, neither good nor bad itself: it takes whatever *character* or disgrace gets attached.
name.oewn-14462254-n.reasoning: Too long at 27 words; 'what a person is held to be' and 'carrying no verdict of its own' made it hard. Kept the neutral charge, 'plainest', and the contrast with *character* and disgrace.

repute.oewn-14461591-n.tone: The same high respect and honor as *reputation*, said in a more formal way.
repute.oewn-14461591-n.reasoning: Used the grammar term 'register' and the hard words 'esteem' and 'elevated'. Kept the comparison with *reputation* and the point that repute is the more formal of the two. 'Esteem' became 'respect'.

patron.oewn-10427699-n.tone: Approving, but the praise is for backing or speaking up for something, not for getting a person out of trouble.
patron.oewn-10427699-n.reasoning: Too long at 28 words, and it used 'championed' and 'advocacy'. Kept both parts of the gloss (supports or champions), with 'speaking up for' standing in for champions, and kept the contrast with helping a person in trouble ('relief').

deliverer.oewn-10573233-n.tone: The grandest and most urgent of the three: it names rescue from harm or danger, not the encouragement of *uncle*.
deliverer.oewn-10573233-n.reasoning: Too long at 26 words, and 'elevated' is hard. Kept 'most elevated' (as 'grandest'), 'most urgent', both parts of the gloss's harm or danger, and the contrast with *uncle*.

pride.oewn-00759528-n.tone: Here a fault, not a virtue: self-esteem grown too big and past all reason, serious enough to be one of the deadly sins.
pride.oewn-00759528-n.reasoning: Too long at 28 words. 'Past all proportion' became 'too big' (for inordinate) and 'unreasonable' became 'past all reason'. Kept the vice-not-virtue contrast and the deadly sins. 'Vice' became 'fault'.

arrogance.oewn-04895107-n.tone: A flat accusation: the swollen self-esteem of *pride* turned outward, as an overbearing, superior manner toward those it looks down on.
arrogance.oewn-04895107-n.reasoning: Too long at 27 words. 'Stopped being inward' became 'turned outward', and 'those it counts as inferior' became 'those it looks down on'. Kept the contrast with *pride* and 'flat accusation'. 'Overbearing' stays as the one hard word because it is the gloss's own term and 'bossy' would weaken it.

appearance.oewn-00756620-n.tone: The mildest word here for faking it: the fault is the wish to look good, where *pretence* blames the falseness itself.
appearance.oewn-00756620-n.reasoning: Too long at 25 words. 'Falsehood' became 'falseness'. Kept 'mildest' and the contrast with *pretence*: appearance blames the motive, pretence blames the falseness.

show.oewn-00756620-n.tone: Sees the same pretending to impress as an act put on for an audience, with more scorn for the performance than *appearance* has.
show.oewn-00756620-n.reasoning: Hard words: 'pretence' became 'pretending', 'onlookers' became 'an audience', and 'sneer' became 'scorn'. Kept the staged-for-watchers picture and the comparison with *appearance*: more contempt than appearance.

affectation.oewn-00757016-n.tone: A charge of deliberate faking or of overdoing it, so the fault is excess as much as falseness.
affectation.oewn-00757016-n.reasoning: Hard words: 'pretence' became 'faking' and 'falsity' became 'falseness'. The old note said the pretence is 'both' calculated and overdone, but the gloss says 'deliberate pretense OR exaggerated display', so the new note keeps the gloss's 'or'. That is the one place I did not follow the old wording. Kept the point that the fault is excess as much as falseness.

pretence.oewn-00756299-n.tone: The flat, general word for putting up a false front, without the wish to impress that softens *appearance*; British spelling.
pretence.oewn-00756299-n.reasoning: Too long at 27 words, with two contrasts. I kept the named one, *appearance* (no flattering motive, which the gloss supports by leaving out any motive). I dropped the unnamed 'no charge of overdoing it'. 'Flattering motive' became 'wish to impress'. Kept the British spelling note.

purpose.oewn-05991037-n.tone: The weightiest plain word for a wanted outcome: it gives the planned action its reason, where *aim* only gives it a direction.
purpose.oewn-05991037-n.reasoning: Too long at 29 words. Dropped 'frames that outcome as'. Kept 'weightiest', the reason-for-planned-action idea from the gloss, and the reason-versus-direction contrast with *aim*.

intention.oewn-05991037-n.tone: Puts the outcome in the person's own mind, so it holds even if nothing is done, unlike *target*, something that can be hit.
intention.oewn-05991037-n.reasoning: Too long at 31 words, and 'anticipated' and 'attainable' are hard. Kept the in-the-mind point, 'holds whether or not anything is done', and the contrast with *target*. 'Attainable thing to be hit' became 'something that can be hit'.

object.oewn-05990115-n.tone: Dry and formal: the goal as a definite thing to get, one believed within reach, without *target*'s sense of hit or miss.
object.oewn-05990115-n.reasoning: Too long at 28 words. 'Believed gettable' became 'believed within reach', which keeps the gloss's attainability. Kept 'dry and formal' and the contrast with *target*.

destination.oewn-05990653-n.tone: Makes the outcome the final one that everything else serves, and brings the picture of a journey's end that *object* lacks.
destination.oewn-05990653-n.reasoning: Too long at 25 words, and 'ultimate' and 'figure' are harder than needed. 'Ultimate' became 'final' and 'figure' became 'picture'. Kept the contrast with *object*.

target.oewn-05990115-n.tone: The sharpest of these: the reachable outcome becomes a thing to hit, so falling short counts as a miss.
target.oewn-05990115-n.reasoning: Flagged for 'registers' (used as a verb). It became 'counts as'. 'Attainable' became 'reachable' and 'struck' became 'hit'. Kept 'sharpest' and the hit-or-miss picture.

inform.oewn-00834860-v.tone: Makes the act a role: you are not someone who spoke but an informer, and the role carries a faint stain *tell* lacks.
inform.oewn-00834860-v.reasoning: Too long at 31 words. 'Taint' became 'stain', and 'rather than an occasion' is now carried by 'someone who spoke'. Kept the role-not-act point, 'faint' (which fits charge -1), and the contrast with *tell*.

spite.oewn-04849746-n.tone: Ill will that covers plain nastiness as well as a real wish to harm, so it can bite without the threat *malice* carries.
spite.oewn-04849746-n.reasoning: Too long at 27 words, with 'malevolence' and 'malicious'. These became 'ill will' and 'a real wish to harm'. Kept the range from nasty to malicious that the gloss gives, 'can bite', and the contrast with *malice*'s threat.

wickedness.oewn-00746935-n.tone: Condemns the same conduct with preachy relish, as if the wrong were knowingly enjoyed, not just done: more vivid than the bare *evil*.
wickedness.oewn-00746935-n.reasoning: Hard words: 'moralizing' became 'preachy' and 'savoured' became 'enjoyed'. 'Fuller-blooded' also became 'more vivid'. Kept the relish, the knowingly-enjoyed idea, and the contrast with the bare *evil*.
